description: Process Manager page — manages spawned child processes with lifecycle controls, log viewing (live ring buffer + historical PG sessions), cross-session search, project scanning, and AI-assisted error diagnosis. Processes are managed by the primary runner; secondary runners proxy their actions. Live output streams via Tauri events into a 2000-line virtualized ring buffer; historical sessions are persisted to PostgreSQL (process_sessions + process_session_output) and browseable via a dropdown picker.

groups.name: Process Inventory and Status Awareness
groups.description: The Process Manager page provides users with a real-time inventory of all processes managed by the runner. Users need to immediately see how many processes are configured, how many are currently running, and the health status of each. The page displays a process list on the left with status indicators (stopped, starting, running, healthy, stopping, failed), PIDs, uptime counters, error counts, and category labels. This overview lets users quickly assess whether their development environment services are all healthy or if something needs attention. The running/total count in the header provides a quick pulse check without needing to scan every row.

assertions.description: Users can identify the Process Manager page and see a clear heading along with a running/total process count summary that communicates the overall health of managed services at a glance

Users can see a list of all configured processes with their names, current status badges, PIDs for running processes, uptime duration, error counts, and category labels, allowing quick assessment of each service
When no processes are configured, users see a helpful empty state that guides them to add their first process configuration rather than showing a blank screen

When the user is viewing the Process Manager from a secondary/test runner (not the primary), a 'Proxied' notice appears explaining that actions are forwarded to the primary runner on a specific port. This sets user expectations that process state is shared across runners.
assertions.precondition: The current runner is a secondary instance (QONTINUI_INSTANCE_NAME is set)

groups.name: Process Lifecycle Controls
groups.description: Users need granular control over the lifecycle of each managed process. For stopped processes, they should be able to start them with a single click. For running processes, they need stop and restart capabilities. Processes that are stopped should also be deletable from the configuration. These controls must be immediately accessible in the process list row without requiring navigation to a detail view, enabling rapid response when a service crashes or needs cycling. The UI must prevent destructive actions on running processes (no delete while running) and provide confirmation for irreversible operations like deletion.

assertions.description: Users can start a stopped process with a single click, bringing the service online without needing to open a terminal or navigate to another interface
Users can stop or restart running processes directly from the process list, enabling quick service cycling when code changes need to be picked up or a process is misbehaving
Users can delete process configurations that are no longer needed, with a confirmation prompt to prevent accidental removal of important service definitions
Users can add new process configurations manually by clicking an Add Process button, which opens a configuration editor for specifying command, arguments, working directory, and other settings

groups.name: Process Output and Diagnostics
groups.description: When a user selects a process from the list, the right panel should display the process output (stdout and stderr) in real-time. This log viewer is the primary diagnostic tool for understanding why a process failed or what it is currently doing. Users need to see timestamped output lines with visual distinction between stdout and stderr streams. For processes that have errors, an AI-powered fix feature should be available that analyzes the error output and provides actionable remediation suggestions, turning the process manager from a passive viewer into an active troubleshooting tool.

assertions.description: Users can select a process to view its real-time output in a dedicated panel, providing visibility into what the process is doing or why it failed without needing to open external log files

criteria.textContent: Select a process to view its output

assertions.description: Users can invoke AI-powered error analysis on a failing process, which examines the stderr output and process configuration to suggest specific fixes, accelerating diagnosis of complex service failures

Users can scan a workspace directory to automatically discover project processes and generate suggested configurations, eliminating the need to manually configure each service for a multi-project workspace

groups.name: Process Output Virtualized Rendering
groups.description: The process output viewer uses react-window virtual scrolling to render only visible log lines. This prevents OOM crashes when processes produce extensive output (e.g., 240K+ lines, 48MB). The viewer maintains a 2000-line in-memory buffer, auto-scrolls to follow new output, and supports search filtering.

assertions.description: The process output viewer uses virtualized rendering — only visible lines plus a 20-line overscan buffer are rendered in the DOM, not all 2000 buffered lines. Scrolling is smooth even with maximum buffer size. The line count indicator shows the total number of buffered lines.
assertions.precondition: A process is selected and has produced output

assertions.description: New output lines automatically scroll the viewer to the bottom when the user is already at the bottom (auto-scroll mode). When the user scrolls up to inspect earlier output, auto-scroll pauses and a 'Scroll to bottom' button appears. Clicking it re-enables auto-scroll.
assertions.precondition: Process is running and producing output, user has scrolled up

assertions.description: The search input filters visible output lines by text content when 'All sessions' toggle is off. The filtered result set is also virtualized. Clearing the search restores the full buffered output. The placeholder text is 'Search output...' in this mode.
assertions.precondition: A process is selected and the All sessions toggle is off

assertions.description: Viewing a process with extensive output (thousands of lines) does not cause the webview to crash with 'Error code: Out of Memory'. The page remains responsive.

groups.name: Historical Session Picker
groups.description: The process output viewer's toolbar includes a session picker dropdown that lets the user switch between the live ring-buffer view and historical sessions persisted in the runner's PostgreSQL database (process_sessions + process_session_output). The runner's event loop writes every output line to PG in batches (50 lines or 500ms), so every process restart creates a new session that can be browsed after the process has stopped. The picker lists 'Live' as the first option followed by up to 20 recent historical sessions (for the currently selected process config), each labeled with a relative time and the session's final exit status. Selecting a historical session swaps the live event stream for a batch fetch of that session's output; selecting 'Live' re-subscribes to the Tauri process-output event. This group specifies that the picker is present and correctly populated for the selected process.

assertions.description: When a process is selected, a session picker dropdown is present in the output viewer toolbar. It is rendered as a native <select> element with at least one option ('Live').
assertions.precondition: A process is selected from the process list

assertions.description: The session picker dropdown has a 'Live' option as its first entry, which is the default selection for a freshly-selected process. This option corresponds to the in-memory ring buffer view that streams new output via Tauri events.
assertions.precondition: A process is selected from the process list

assertions.description: After the selected process has run at least once and then stopped, the session picker should include historical session options populated from GET /api/v1/files/browse (or the equivalent Tauri command). Each historical entry displays a relative timestamp ('2h ago', 'yesterday') and the final state ('exit 0', 'failed 1'). This is how users access logs from prior process runs after a restart.
assertions.precondition: The selected process has stopped at least once (has historical sessions in the database)

assertions.description: Selecting a historical session in the picker should swap the output area from the live Tauri event stream to a DB fetch via get_process_session_output_from_db. The line count indicator updates to reflect the historical session's line count. Selecting 'Live' again re-subscribes to the event stream. A verification workflow can check this by comparing the displayed lines before/after switching — historical selections show fixed content, Live shows real-time updates.
assertions.precondition: The selected process has at least one historical session

groups.name: Cross-Session Search
groups.description: The output viewer toolbar includes an 'All sessions' toggle button next to the search input. When active (visually highlighted cyan), the search input's placeholder changes from 'Search output...' to 'Search all sessions...' and typing triggers a backend call to search_process_logs, which runs an ILIKE query across every persisted session's output in the runner's PostgreSQL database. Results appear in a hits panel replacing the normal output view, each row showing the session ID prefix, process name, timestamp, and the matching log line. Clicking a hit jumps to that session in the picker and switches the view to that session's full content. This turns the process manager into a full-history log search tool, not just a live viewer. Toggling the button off restores the regular in-buffer filter.

assertions.description: An 'All sessions' toggle button is present in the output viewer toolbar when a process is selected. Clicking it switches the search mode from in-buffer filtering to cross-session DB search.
assertions.precondition: A process is selected from the process list

assertions.description: When the 'All sessions' toggle is off, the search input's placeholder is 'Search output...'. When the toggle is on, the placeholder changes to 'Search all sessions...'. This is the visual cue that search scope has changed from the live buffer to the cross-session DB query.
assertions.precondition: A process is selected from the process list

assertions.description: When the 'All sessions' toggle is on and the search query returns no matches, the output area displays the message 'No matches across sessions.' in the zinc-600 text color. This distinguishes 'no hits' from 'no output' (the empty-state message for live mode is 'No output yet').
assertions.precondition: All sessions toggle is on, search query returns no hits

assertions.description: When the cross-session search returns matches, the output area renders one row per hit. Each row shows: the row timestamp (dimmed, text-zinc-600), the process name, the first 8 characters of the session_id, and the matching line (stderr hits in red). A 'N hits across sessions' header is shown above the list. Clicking a hit should switch to that session in the session picker (setSelectedSessionId) and clear the toggle.
assertions.precondition: All sessions toggle is on, search query returns at least one hit

assertions.description: Cross-session search hits must contain a session_id that exists in the session picker's dropdown for the current process. Clicking a hit should navigate to a session that exists — dead links (pointing to a session not present in the picker) indicate either a config_id mismatch between the picker query and the search query, or that the session has been cleaned up. A verification workflow can cross-check this by comparing the session_ids in the hits against the options in the dropdown.
assertions.precondition: All sessions toggle is on, search query returns hits for the selected process

groups.name: Process Log Persistence — Algorithm Correctness
groups.description: The process log DB persistence feature writes every stdout/stderr line to PostgreSQL tables (process_sessions + process_session_output) via a batched writer task in the ManagedProcess event loop. This group defines what CORRECT output looks like from that persistence algorithm, verifiable from the page: the session picker reflects every process run, the historical session content matches what was previously shown live, the line counts are consistent between live and historical views, and zombie 'running' sessions from previous runner crashes are cleaned up on startup so the picker doesn't show stale entries.

assertions.description: Each time a process starts, a new session row is created; when it stops, the row's state becomes 'stopped' (clean exit) or 'failed' (non-zero exit code). The session picker shows exactly one historical entry per past run of the currently selected process. If a user starts-stops a process 3 times, the picker should show 3 historical entries (plus 'Live' if currently running) — not 2 (missing write) or 4 (duplicate create).
assertions.precondition: User has run the selected process multiple times

assertions.description: When a running process is selected in Live mode and the user observes some specific output lines, then the process stops and the user selects the just-ended historical session from the picker, the displayed lines in the historical view should be a superset of what was shown in Live mode (Live is capped at 2000 lines; historical includes all 50K persisted lines). Content MUST match for the overlapping range — if Live showed 'ERROR foo' at 14:30:05, the historical session must also show 'ERROR foo' at 14:30:05. A mismatch indicates the batched writer dropped or reordered lines.

target.label: Line count indicator (compare live vs historical)

assertions.precondition: A process has been observed in Live mode and then stopped

assertions.description: After a runner restart, the session picker should not show any historical entries labeled 'running' — those would be zombie sessions from the previous runner instance that died without a clean shutdown. The orphaned-session cleanup task in main.rs runs at startup and marks any such sessions as 'failed' with a stopped_at timestamp. If the picker shows 'running' entries for the currently-selected process but the process itself is in 'stopped' or 'failed' state, the cleanup failed to run.
assertions.precondition: The runner has been restarted since the process last ran and the selected process is currently stopped

assertions.description: Session state labels in the picker should match the corresponding run outcome: a clean exit ('exit 0') appears as 'exit 0' in the label, a non-zero exit appears as 'failed N', and sessions marked failed by the orphan cleanup appear as 'failed ?' (unknown exit code). Invariant: a session in the picker labeled 'exit 0' MUST have exit_code=0 in the DB; 'failed N' MUST have exit_code=N>0.
assertions.precondition: The selected process has historical sessions with various exit codes

groups.name: Visual Design and Text Legibility
groups.description: The Process Manager uses the runner's standard dark theme with zinc grays, cyan accents for primary actions, and red/yellow/green for status indication. Text must be legible against the panel backgrounds — muted text uses zinc-500, primary text uses zinc-200, headings use zinc-200. The toolbar uses zinc-900 backgrounds with white/10 borders. Buttons in the toolbar follow the existing runner style: small xs text, bg-zinc-800 for secondary, bg-cyan-900/40 with border-cyan-700/50 for primary (Add Process), and the 'All sessions' toggle uses bg-cyan-900/30 with text-cyan-300 when active.

assertions.description: The 'Process Manager' heading uses the text-zinc-200 color token and is clearly legible against the zinc-900/bg-card background. The cyan icon next to it provides a visual anchor.

When the 'All sessions' toggle is active, the button has a visible cyan highlight (text-cyan-300, border-cyan-700/50, bg-cyan-900/30). When inactive, it uses text-zinc-500 with border-white/10. This visual state change is the primary indicator of which search scope is active.
assertions.expected: cyan-700/50 when active, white/10 when inactive

assertions.description: The search input's placeholder text (zinc-600) is visible against the bg-zinc-900 background but clearly distinct from the actual input text color (zinc-300 when typed). This ensures users can distinguish 'placeholder hint' from 'my typed query' at a glance.

Output lines from stderr streams are rendered in red (text-red-400/80), distinguishing them from stdout lines (text-zinc-300). This applies both in Live mode and in historical session views, and in the cross-session search hits panel where red highlights stderr matches.
assertions.precondition: Selected process has produced stderr lines

states.description: The 'All sessions' toggle is active (cyan highlight). The search input placeholder is 'Search all sessions...'. Typing triggers search_process_logs; results appear as a hits panel. The normal virtualized output list is hidden.
